subject: Replicate multipleGroup() DIF detection result by DIF()

messages.author: 20d04914716d9d40
messages.subject: Replicate multipleGroup() DIF detection result by DIF()
parts:
Hi Phil, I have two questions about the DIF function. Thank you for writing such a helpful package! 
My first question is when we were trying to run likelihood ratio DIF testing procedure, we first compute step by step by using the multipleGroup function in mirt. The code we used is:

itemname1 <- colnames(Resp1)
Sex1=as.character(Sex)
models <- 'F1 = 1-10'
refmod <- multipleGroup(Resp1, models, group = Sex1, SE=TRUE,invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var', itemname1))
# loop over items 
estmodels1 <- vector('list', ncol(Resp1))
for(i in 1:ncol(Resp1))
  estmodels1[[i]] <- multipleGroup(Resp1, models, group = Sex1, verbose = FALSE, calcNull=FALSE,invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var', itemname1[-i]))
(anovas <- lapply(estmodels1, anova, object2=refmod, verbose=FALSE)) 
# family-wise error control
p <- do.call(rbind, lapply(anovas, function(x) x[2, 'p']))
p.adjust(p, method = 'BH')
which(p.adjust(p, method = 'BH')<0.05)  # flagged items are (4,5,6,9,10)

Then we tried to use the DIF function to replicate above result by running:

refmod <- multipleGroup(Resp1, models, group = Sex1, SE=TRUE,invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var', itemname1))
DIF(refmod, which.par = c('a1', 'd'), p.adjust = 'fdr',scheme = 'drop')  #the flagged DIF items are (4,5,6)

However, the result computed by DIF was different from the one by multipleGroup. We expected DIF, as a "wrapper to the multipleGroup function", to generate the same result as the multipleGroup function. May I ask why would this happen?

My second question is if we want to equate two groups by leaving "free_means" and "free_var" out of the invariance argument, what constraint would be set on the mean and variance of the two groups (like constrain the mean to be zero and variance to be one)?

Thank you in advance for your help!

-Ruoyi
